claim_scope: two equal-shape raw action tensors can encode different units and gripper polarity
schema-aware adapters align the procedural actions while naive raw pooling changes semantics
records with missing embodiment metadata or missing/stale adapter fingerprints are rejected before mixture construction
changes to action conversion semantics change the deterministic adapter schema fingerprint
dataset-, episode-, and transition-uniform sampling produce different source exposure on the same authored episode lengths
dropping incomplete three-step action windows removes the short source from eligible loss windows despite its nonzero raw-transition share

code.config: standard-library v4 canonical action adapter, mixture-denominator, and action-window exposure fixture

data.name: procedural arm_a and arm_b action records

limitations: two scalar action fields and two synthetic tasks
hand-authored invertible adapters rather than learned cross-embodiment alignment
naive pooling error is an interface counterexample, not measured negative transfer
no images, language, robot dynamics, policy training, or closed-loop evaluation
schema fingerprint is deterministic cache identity, not authentication, data integrity, or controller validation
mixture exposure uses two hand-authored datasets, four episodes, fourteen transitions, and six eligible windows rather than a real training pipeline
contiguous L-H+1 window counting assumes stride one and drop-tail with no padding, masks, sampling replacement, distributed sharding, or gradient weighting
